text:
Some women are fixer types, which can create the opposite pattern. Before me, Bee had housed and supported a boyfriend who was totally broke and crazy, for a while. Later she blamed herself for staying through that, and I agree, it wasn't appropriate. It's not the same as helping carry somebody through a temporary incapacity, like she did with my knee.

What I still want to know is whether she’ll love me through a stretch when I’m the one who needs carrying.
reader: someone reading an essay on romance for advice they can use in their own dating and relationships

sentences.s: Some women are fixer types, which can create the opposite pattern.
sentences.payoff: they learn to watch for a partner who fixes people, a pattern that goes the other way from the one before.
sentences.follows: it follows the paragraph before by naming 'the opposite pattern', which that paragraph must have described.
sentences.link: none: opens the section's next case and points back through 'the opposite pattern', beyond its first six words

sentences.s: Before me, Bee had housed and supported a boyfriend who was totally broke and crazy, for a while.
sentences.payoff: they see a concrete case of a fixer in Bee, who supported a broke and unstable boyfriend.
sentences.follows: it gives the example of a fixer type.

sentences.s: Later she blamed herself for staying through that, and I agree, it wasn't appropriate.
sentences.payoff: they learn that even a fixer saw the staying as a mistake, so it isn't a model to copy.
sentences.follows: it gives Bee's own later verdict on S2.

sentences.s: It's not the same as helping carry somebody through a temporary incapacity, like she did with my knee.
sentences.payoff: they can tell supporting a person who needs a rescuer from carrying a partner through a temporary setback.
sentences.follows: it draws the line after S3 between that staying and the knee.

sentences.s: What I still want to know is whether she’ll love me through a stretch when I’m the one who needs carrying.
sentences.payoff: they see what he still wants to find out: whether she would love him when he is the one who needs help, as he helped carry others
sentences.follows: it turns the paragraph before's "helping carry somebody through a temporary incapacity" around to himself
sentences.link: What I still want to know

placement: It stands after a paragraph about a first pattern, so S1 is read against that paragraph; once past S1 the order is case, verdict, distinction, open question.

opens.first_sentence: Some women are fixer types, which can create the opposite pattern.
opens.why_reading: It tells the reader a different kind of partner, the fixer, makes a different problem, but not which pattern it is the opposite of.

same_point: 'like with my knee' appears in both S4 and S5, and both say staying through a temporary stretch is good.

question_text.Q1: Why am I reading this sentence, and do I know it before I have to work through it? (the point first, in each sentence and each paragraph; a study after the question it answers; a term explained where it is first used, never in a sentence after it)
question_text.Q2: What is each instruction for, said in the reader's terms, and is it something the helper does ("have someone go with them"), not a rule stated as a fact ("someone goes with them")?
question_text.Q3: Which thing exactly? (pools of water, not water; any substance, not anything)
question_text.Q4: What does each word act on, or mean here? (adjunct remedy; known-genuine) Is every term a high-school graduate wouldn't know (enterocytes, BPC-157) explained once, where it is first used, and common ones (a vitamin) left alone? Is each mechanism explained by what it does in the reader's experience (dopamine "for motivation (by showing us what is important to pay attention to)"; DeltaFosB "preventing that learning from really clicking"), not by where it sits or what it looks like ("a chemical blanket", "the slower one underneath")? (E375)
question_text.Q5: Why does each sentence follow from the one before? (every but, so, because and this has what it turns on)
question_text.Q6: Is this the order the reader is thinking in, and does each idea sit next to what it continues?
question_text.Q7: Does each fact help this reader now, in their case (the same kind of thing they face, not just the same topic)?
question_text.Q8: Does each item belong in the group it is put in?
question_text.Q9: Is anything compressed? (one step a sentence, the small words that carry the relation, no space before mg)
